title: Pitik: A Cebuano-Binisaya Intent-Based Chatbot for Cardiovascular Disease Patient Profiling and Risk Factor Recommendations
authors: Cedeno, J.G.; Manteza, A.E.; Nacar, N.C.; Umbukan, M.P.; Muana, C.G.; Vasay, M.J.; Benablo, C.I.P.; Adlaon, K.M.M.
tldr: Pitik is a Cebuano-Binisaya intent-based chatbot developed to profile cardiovascular disease patients and assess risk factors using Gricean Maxims for communication validation.
problem_and_motivation: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death in the Philippines, yet patient profiling in rural areas remains manual and relies on non-standardized records. No Cebuano-Binisaya healthcare chatbots or datasets exist.
approach: Built a schema-guided dialogue dataset from 100 Cebuano-Binisaya-speaking participants.
Used Google DialogFlow as the conversational platform with webhook integration.
Applied Gricean Maxims (quantity, quality, relation, manner) as the framework for evaluating conversational acceptability.
Developed Pre-Intent and Post-Intent Matching algorithms within a Diag-Ex framework across three software iterations.
Trained and compared Naive Bayes, SVM, MLP, and RNN classifiers for intent recognition.
Evaluated system quality using Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with Performance, Humanness, and Accessibility criteria.
Computed cardiovascular risk using the Framingham formula.
findings: num: SVM achieved 73% accuracy in Smoking/Alcohol classification, outperforming NB (68%), MLP (68%), and RNN (60%).
num: Naive Bayes and SVM both achieved approximately 70% accuracy in Diet/Exercise classification.
num: Accessibility improved from 22% to 96% across iterations through suggestion chips and tooltips.
num: Performance improved from 65% to 79% in the third iteration with Naive Bayes post-intent matching.
num: Gricean Maxim violations decreased significantly from second to third iteration across all four maxims.
RNN consistently underperformed across both classification domains, ranging from 57% to 61% across metrics.
AHP analysis weighted Performance at 0.790, Accessibility at 0.133, and Humanness at 0.077.

topics.name: None
topics.justification: Paper addresses healthcare chatbot development and NLP, not personal finance domains.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Contributes to conversational AI applied to healthcare by developing a Cebuano-Binisaya intent-based chatbot for cardiovascular disease patient profiling. Introduces the first schema-guided dialogue dataset tailored to a Philippine regional language for healthcare.
directly_justifies: No topics from the personal finance taxonomy are directly addressed by this paper.
The ML classifier comparison is tangentially relevant to predictive modeling but applied to healthcare.
The AHP evaluation methodology is transferable but used to evaluate chatbot quality, not personal finance.
limits: The paper addresses healthcare informatics and NLP, not personal finance.
The study was not conducted in a financial context.
The ML algorithms compared are applied to a narrow intent-classification domain, not financial forecasting.

limitations: Study was limited to 100 participants not representative of the broader Cebuano-Binisaya population.
No peer review as this is a TechRxiv preprint.
Classification models were tested on only 40 records per domain, a very small evaluation set.
Paper does not address long-term deployment or real-world clinical validation.
remember_this: Pitik is a Cebuano-Binisaya chatbot for cardiovascular disease patient profiling and risk assessment.
SVM achieved the highest accuracy at 73% for Smoking/Alcohol intent classification among four models.
Accessibility improved from 22% to 96% across iterations through suggestion chips and tooltips.
The paper uses Gricean Maxims as a framework to evaluate chatbot conversational quality.
No digitized Cebuano-Binisaya healthcare dataset previously existed for this domain.
